column1: # Hand-made file boundaries and names, merged by tools/split_files.py.
# A row forces a file to start at `text` with this name (renaming the
# generated file if one already starts there); if the generator started a
# file with this name elsewhere, that start is dropped, so a row can move a
# file's start. `rodata` forces where its .rodata starts ('-': inferred).

column4: evidence

Moves the start from 0x101CCC. 0x101CCC-0x102488 read the pad through BedPad's socket (+0x20: scePad2GetState, scePad2Read) and fill or read BedPad fields (sticks at +0x7E..+0x81, floats at +0x4C..+0x58), calling each other: BedPad methods, so they end bed/bedpad. 0x102490 is the first function that touches no BedPad (looks up a game table, like the utl/utlgame.cpp functions after it).

Moves the start from 0x100320. That function zeroes m_depth (+0x50) and m_stack (+0x10..+0x4F), BedSubMode's exact layout, and its only caller is the constructor at 0x1360A0 (mag/magscene2), right after zeroing that member's m_cur and m_stack inline: it is a BedSubMode method, so it ends bed/bedsubmode. 0x100354 is the first function with bed/bedmemory.cpp asserts.

Moves the start from 0x101718. That function zeroes a 0x1C-byte object whose fields (+0x00..+0x18) are the heap object bed/bedmemory works on (0x100354 initialises the same fields) and is only called from a static initialiser, on the global heap later passed to bedmemory's allocator 0x100C84: it is bedmemory's heap constructor. 0x101738 is BedPfh::clear, called by 0x101750 (the first function with bed/bedpfh asserts) and by every BedPfh user right before it.
Engine graphics library (C): I3D_BIN/I3D_I3M/I3D_I3C format IDs in its .rodata; called from dog/, mag/, effects and menus. Every function is 8-aligned (built with other flags than the game).
Sound library: from here on callers are snd/ and game/ (sound manager); 0x237D00 is the first function calling into this region, the ones before it are called by i3d.

The functions between utlIsTcc (utl/utlmisc) and utl/utlfile: VU0 vftoi15 helpers, a text tokenizer, a frame counter (0x105B3C, the only user of the first .data word, 0x295F00), the global operator new/delete and wrappers of the global heap (the BedMemory at 0x6E9800). No assert or .rodata names them; they may be the tail of utl/utlmisc or several files.

Moves the start from 0x1056E8. The asserts of 0x105E50 are at utl/utlfile.cpp lines 15-16 (those of 0x105F0C at 36-37), so it is the file's first function: lines 1-12 leave no room for another. Only these two functions use the file's .rodata (0x2E7760).

Moves the start from 0x106010. 0x1060E8 has the first utl/utlfind.cpp assert, at line 22, and the next functions assert every 12-14 lines: no room for two functions before it. The two before it are generic string helpers (a case-insensitive compare called from mag/magloader, a bounded upper-case copy called from debug/motnamecnv, with utlStrCopy's parameters), so they end utl/utlfile; the rest of utl/utlfind serves MagLifeBwnCtrl.

The functions between utl/utlfind and DogMotionBlend's methods: a sound-id lookup for SndMan (the only user of the .data table at 0x295F08), a wrapper around an i3d call, and vector/angle math over sceVu0 and atanf, called from dog/, mag/ and effects. No assert or .rodata names them; they may be the tail of utl/utlfind or several files.

Moves the start from 0x106658. 0x10737C is the first function that works on a DogMotionBlend (m_main at +0x00, m_motion at +0x1C, like 0x107560, whose asserts at dog/dogmotionblend.cpp lines 83-87 name those fields); every function before it is unrelated math, sound or i3d code.

Moves the start from 0x10F5E4. 0x10F860 has the first dog/dogcamera.cpp assert, at line 22; the functions before it are DogActor's eye methods (unk/0010F3A4), whose float table at 0x2E84B0 comes right before the "dog/dogcamera.cpp" string (0x2E84C0) that starts dogcamera's .rodata.

Moves the start from 0x108588. 0x108588 is DogMotionBlend's constructor (the reset values of DogMotionBlend::validate, plus m_speedRatio = 1 and m_tickTime = -1), right after DogMotionBlend's last method; DogActor's constructors call it for their two DogMotionBlend members (+0x1E4, +0x2C4). It ends dog/dogmotionblend.

DogActor's eye methods (material lookup by the name "eye", blinking: fields +0x470..+0x494). Their .rodata ("eye" at 0x2E8488, the frame tables at 0x2E8490 and 0x2E84B0) comes after the RTTI names ("9DogEntity", "8DogActor") and the asserts of DogActor's inline methods (getMotion, getBlendMotion), which end dog/dogactor's .rodata because a translation unit emits them last: they are a file of their own. 0x10F2DC, right before, asserts at dog/dogactor.cpp line 4614.

Moves the start from 0x10F944. 0x10F944-0x10FC28 work on DogCamera's fields (a move to a target position and rotation over a number of frames at +0x130..+0x1D0; the field of view at +0x140 that DogCamera::save keeps, and +0x144) and are only called on the scene's camera (+0x2AB70, like save and restore); 0x10FAC0's lens table (0x2E84F8, 13 floats from 0 to 180) follows dogcamera's strings in .rodata. 0x10FC7C (sets the rotation, called on models, actors and the camera) is the first function that only uses DogEntity; dogentity's .rodata starts with "dog/dogentity.cpp" at 0x2E8530.

Keeps the start; moves .rodata from 0x2E8558. "11DogEntityEx" (0x2E8558) and "9DogEntity" (0x2E8568) are the RTTI names dog/dogentity emits last (DogEntityEx's key method, reset, is defined there); dog/doglightpool's .rodata starts with "dog/doglightpool.cpp" at 0x2E8578.

Moves the start from 0x113F28. 0x113F28 rebuilds DogLight's i3d light list (+0x00..+0x3F) from its own fields (light arrays at +0x44..+0x58, counts at +0x5C.., the type mask at +0x74, the dirty flag at +0x78 that dog/doglight's functions set) and copies the default ambient (0, 0, 0, 1) at 0x2E8B00, which follows dog/doglight's strings and comes before "dog/dogmodel.cpp" (0x2E8B10): it ends dog/doglight. 0x114034 and 0x1141C8 use no DogLight field, string or constant; they stay with dog/dogmodel, whose first assert is at 0x11440C (line 272).

Moves the start from 0x1160A8, and .rodata from 0x2E8D90: dog/dogmodel (with DogModel's key method, transform) emits "8DogModel" there, then the strings of its out-of-line inline methods ("p", "n>0" at 0x2E8DA0, which the linkonce assignTex and getNodeIndexByName copies use) and "9DogEntity"; dog/dogtexinfo's .rodata starts with "dog/dogtexinfo.cpp" at 0x2E8DC0. 0x1160A8, 0x116130 (DogModel::func_00116130, which DogActor calls on its own model) and 0x11618C are DogModel methods: they allocate and step the timer at +0x16C and copy the user values at +0x170 to the model's i3d root (+0x11C). 0x1161E4 has the first dog/dogtexinfo.cpp assert (line 47, m_tex_info).

Moves the start from 0x11764C: 0x11764C is an empty DogTexInfo method (DogModel::vfunc14 calls it on its DogTexInfo when assigning the textures fails), so it ends dog/dogtexinfo; 0x117654 and 0x1176BC count frames in mag/magsystem's .data (0x296194) and re-enable interrupts. mag/magsystem's .rodata starts with "mag/magsystem.cpp" at 0x2E9050, right after dog/dogtexinfo's last assert string ("m_num_tex > 0").

Moves the start from 0x11948C, and .rodata from 0x2E93D8. 0x11948C calls a method of MagSystem's scene (+0x12540) like the 30 wrappers before it, so it ends mag/magsystem. 0x1194B4 (clears a 0x10-byte link) and 0x1194C8 (unlinks it from a list whose head is +0x400) are list helpers of the life pods that 0x11950C (first mag/maglifeman.cpp assert, line 103, thePod1) links. The 13 chapter pack paths ("data/ch/00/CHAP00.RPK".."CHAP12.RPK", 0x2E93D8-0x2E950F) are only reached through the .data table at 0x2961A8, which mag/magsystem reads (0x119178, 0x119218): a file-scope table, whose strings a file emits after its functions' .rodata (after magsystem's jump tables, which end at 0x2E93D8); mag/maglifeman's .rodata starts with "mag/maglifeman.cpp" at 0x2E9510.

Moves the start from 0x104970. 0x104970, 0x104AD0 and 0x104C44 are three more cone tests like 0x1046B4 (utl/utlbtl): the same fields (+0x4 type, +0xC self, +0x10 target, +0x14 aim, +0x18 size), the same inline sqrtf, normalise, dot product, acosf/tanf; they only differ in the type values and distances, and use no string. 0x104E1C is the first TIM2 function (sums the picture sizes of a TM2 header); the first utl/utltm2.cpp assert (line 125) is the next-but-one function.
Moves the start from 0x13F07C. The asserts of magscenelight.cpp start on line 32, at 0x13F49C, and leave no room for the twelve methods before it (game state and message box, not lights).

Keeps the start; moves .rodata from 0x2E9660. "19MagLifeControlChara", "16MagLifeBillboard", "8MagLife0" and "7MagLife" (0x2E9660-0x2E96A9) are the RTTI names mag/maglife emits last: it defines the key methods of MagLifeControlChara (vfunc09, 0x119FE0) and MagLifeBillboard (live, 0x11A8F4), and the inline __tf of their bases. mag/maglifepc emits only its own "9MagLifePC" and "8MagLife0" (0x2EA1E8), since MagLifeControlChara's RTTI is mag/maglife's; its .rodata starts at 0x2E96B0 ("base").

Keeps the start; moves .rodata from 0x2FC418. Compiled, gamtrg's jump tables are 16-aligned (so is its .rodata section), and the game's tables (0x2FC710, 0x2FC7B0, 0x2FD5A0, 0x2FD600) are 16-aligned in memory: the object starts at a multiple of 16, and 0x2FC410 is inside "game/gamstat.cpp" (0x2FC400), so it is 0x2FC420. The 8 bytes at 0x2FC418 (0xFFFF0000 and get_o_oid__7ObjStatPv: a pointer to ObjStat::get_o_oid, used by gamtrg at 0x1D9B78) are the end of game/gamstat's .rodata (found by a Sonnet 5.5 subagent).
